intro: A predictive distribution can assign too little probability to outcomes that matter. Relative entropy measures the expected extra surprise under that mismatch.
task: Compute KL(p || q) in nats while keeping its direction explicit and skipping zero-mass terms from p.
requirements: p and q are probability vectors of equal length. Every q entry must be strictly positive; zero p entries are allowed.
Return sum(p_i*(log(p_i)-log(q_i))) over positive p_i. This is directed: p and q are not interchangeable.
Do not smooth or clip either distribution; reject any zero q entry in this finite-output contract.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: The first argument supplies the averaging weights. Swapping arguments changes the quantity being measured.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Subtract log probabilities instead of first forming a possibly enormous probability ratio.

explanation: KL averages the log ratio using p, so the result asks how q describes outcomes drawn from p. Reversing the arguments changes both the weights and the log ratio.
Zero p terms contribute nothing. The exercise requires positive q everywhere to keep every supported case finite without inventing a smoothing policy.
